scenario: Community search over short user-generated posts, questions, answers, and comments. Main metrics: nDCG and CTR. Priorities include semantic matching, query understanding, retrieval, ranking, and LLM applications in search.

papers.title: Chinese Decision: A Family of Language Models for Single-Pass Probabilistic Decision-Making
papers.authors: Qiang Yan (Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences)
papers.summary: Some applications need candidate probabilities rather than generated explanations. Chinese Decision normalizes candidate-letter logits from a single forward pass for Boolean, categorical, and ordinal decisions. Its completed 0.8B model reaches 72.24% general-domain accuracy on CJ-Bench.
papers.key_insight: Expose candidate probabilities directly when a task only needs a finite decision. This avoids autoregressive answer generation, while calibration and individual prediction changes still require their own evaluation.

papers.title: The Thin Orchestrator: How We Made Our AI Agents More Reliable by Giving the Router Less to Do
papers.summary: A single agent mixed up rules when onboarding data columns across recommendation pipelines. Meta moved routing and reliability checks into a thin orchestrator and isolated domain reasoning in specialist agents. Configuration preparation fell from three to four days manually to under an hour.
papers.key_insight: Keep workflow sequencing deterministic and load domain knowledge only in the relevant specialist. Recombining existing workflows can add capabilities without expanding the central agent’s context.

papers.title: HEM-Med: A Hierarchical Agentic Memory Framework for Safe Multi-Center Medication Recommendation
papers.authors: Min Xiao, Jin Li, Shoujin Wang, Yeguang Zhen, Yishuo Li, Wenpeng Lu
papers.summary: Separate shared experience from local prescribing patterns before generating a medication set. HEM-Med retrieves both memory levels and enforces safety and formulary constraints during decoding. It reports an F1 score of 0.4532 on the multicenter eICU dataset.
papers.key_insight: Keep transferable evidence separate from local preferences. Applying both compatibility and availability constraints during set generation is a useful design for constrained recommendation; the evaluation here is clinical, rather than consumer recommendation.

papers.title: Humanity's Last Choice: A Common Evaluation Standard for Generative Engine Optimization
papers.authors: Qianfeng Wen, Yifan Simon Liu, Difan Jiao, Junda Wu, Di Bai, Jintao Liu, Xidong Wu, Zhenwei Tang
papers.summary: Generative-search optimization studies often allow different source edits, making their results difficult to compare. This position paper organizes edits by layer, action, and target signal, then specifies controlled comparisons. It proposes a protocol rather than reporting a benchmark performance gain.
papers.key_insight: Control edit permissions and optimization budgets before comparing citation gains. A source can become more visible while degrading the original task, so visibility and task quality need separate measurements.

papers.title: Causal Edit Serialization
papers.summary: Text revision often regenerates large amounts of unchanged context. Causal Edit Serialization emits pointer-addressed edit programs inside a causal token stream while retaining the original context. The localization components add approximately 0.34–0.41% parameters at the tested depths.
papers.key_insight: Represent localized revision as an executable program. Separating edit content from source addresses makes transformations inspectable and lets the system retain source context and cached states.

papers.title: LED: Improving Masked Diffusion Language Models by Lookahead Editing
papers.authors: Yuyan Zhou, Zeyuan Yang, Yuxuan Song, Zhicheng Cai, Hongli Yu, Weiying Ma, Hao Zhou, James Kwok
papers.summary: Masked diffusion commits tokens too early to revise poor choices. LED keeps an editable proposal state and refines future predictions before committing them. Its 7B model improves the eight-benchmark average by 11.4 points over standard masked-diffusion supervised fine-tuning.
papers.key_insight: Separate proposal updates from final token commitment. This preserves iterative revision while retaining mask-based training, although extra proposal updates also consume inference compute.

papers.title: On the SPOT: Enhancing Speculative Decoding for Diffusion Language Models via Commit-Order Prediction
papers.authors: Eliezer Shlomi, Eliron Rahimi, Avi Mendelson, Chaim Baskin
papers.summary: Diffusion decoding must predict both tokens and the order in which positions are committed. SPOT learns that order, proposes a tree of continuations, and verifies branches in parallel. Reported peak throughput is 3.2 times standard decoding.
papers.key_insight: Learn the commitment order as well as token content. Prior output distributions contain useful draft tokens, but a verifier still needs to check which proposed state is actually the next target state.

papers.title: Trust but Verify: Designing Region-Inhomogeneous Forward Dynamics for Discrete Diffusion
papers.summary: Observed context can be wrong even when a diffusion model treats it as fixed. Region-dependent corruption teaches the model to detect and revise suspicious context. With 20% uniform-random corruption, infilling token F1 improves by 6.4 points.
papers.key_insight: Observed tokens need not be fully trusted. A small revision allowance helps with obvious corruption, but gains on plausible errors are weaker and were not statistically significant in the reported setting.

papers.title: Prism Attention: Proposal-Refined Index Sharing Mechanism for Efficient LLMs Inference
papers.authors: Zhenxu Tian, Kebin Liu, Zhengwu Yang, Yi Su, Qingqing Dang, Yanlin Sha, Kaipeng Deng, Dianhai Yu, Yanjun Ma, Juntao Li, Min Zhang
papers.summary: Sparse attention can spend much of its savings recomputing token indices across layers. Prism Attention shares coarse proposals and refines them locally for each layer. It reports 3.4-times end-to-end decoding speedup over FlashAttention at a 128K context length.
papers.key_insight: Share candidate regions across layers while allowing local refinement. Stable high-attention cores can be reused, with computation concentrated on changing boundaries instead of recomputing all indices.

papers.title: Accelerating Mamba-2 with High-Performance Forward Pass Kernels in NVIDIA CUDA Tile
papers.summary: Mamba-2 can lose time moving intermediate state between kernels. The authors use cuTile to fuse tiled computation and optimize memory layouts for the forward pass. On B300, the kernels run 1.14–1.82 times faster than the Triton reference.
papers.key_insight: Separate inter-chunk state propagation from intra-chunk computation and keep temporary matrices in registers. These are forward-kernel results; backward computation and other pipeline costs determine end-to-end gains.
